Review date: 2026-07-09. Package version reviewed: TaxaFetch 0.1.0. Review conducted by
Claude Code, using the template in `inst/Code and Domain Review 2.Rmd`. This review
combines findings and fixes in one pass (no separate response document) -- all issues
below were fixed and verified in the same session, with two design decisions (marked
below) made by K. D. Lafferty before implementation.

`devtools::check()`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes. `devtools::test()`: 459 expectations
(up from 434 before this review), 0 failures, 0 errors (2 expected skips, 6 expected
warnings from tests deliberately checking warning messages). `lintr::lint_package()`:
clean.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Code Review

Purpose: To produce high quality code that is well written and organized according to
best coding practices.

### [x] Functionality: The code is readable, organized, and efficient.

Readable and consistently organized across all 24 files -- roxygen documentation,
internal-helper naming (`.` prefix), and `package::function()` cross-package calls follow
the same conventions throughout. No changes needed here.

### [x] Optimizations: No areas needing optimization; documentation is adequate.

No performance concerns found. `fetch_occurrences_by_taxon()` (the newest function,
Session 140) already documents its own known scaling limitation (GBIF's uncharacterized
WKT-complexity ceiling) rather than leaving it undiscovered.

### [x] Coding standards: No errors or bad practices; docstrings and comments are accurate.

Every exported function has complete roxygen (title, `@param` for every argument,
`@return` describing actual structure, `@examples`). Two doc-accuracy gaps were found and
fixed (see File-specific comments): `get_gbif_occurrences()`'s `rank_filter` doc didn't
disclose that it drops `SUBSPECIES`/`VARIETY`/`FORM` records, and `get_keys_from_context()`'s
`matchType` enum and review-advice list didn't mention the real `"LOOKUP_RECOVERED"` value
its own recovery path can return.

### [x] Automated tests: Confirmed passing when run locally.

`devtools::test()`: 459 expectations, 0 failures, 0 errors. (Always use `devtools::test()`,
not bare `testthat::test_dir()`, for this package -- see `TaxaFetch/CLAUDE.md`'s Known
Footguns for why the latter produces false "function not found" failures.)

### [x] Vulnerabilities: One real finding, fixed; see below.

**SSRF via third-party EML metadata (Medium-High, fixed).** `dataone_standardize.R`'s
`.download_data_table()` and `dataone_preview.R`'s `.preview_one_entity()` (via
`.get_content_length()`/`.stream_n_rows()`) took `data_url` verbatim from EML metadata
fetched from the PASTA/EDI repository and used it as the full request URL (host and
scheme included) for HTTP GET/HEAD calls, with no restriction on the destination. Verified
live against a real PASTA record (`edi.1290.9`) that legitimate `dataTable`/`otherEntity`
download URLs consistently resolve to `pasta.lternet.edu`, while other `<online><url>`
entries in the same real record pointed at five different external hosts entirely
(`filelib.wildlife.ca.gov`, `wildlife.ca.gov`, `nrm.dfg.ca.gov`, `usbr.gov`, `doi.org`) --
confirming the attack surface is real, not theoretical: a malformed or malicious EML
record could point `data_url` at an internal address, and this code would fetch it.

*Decision (K. D. Lafferty): add a host allowlist.* Fixed via `.is_trusted_pasta_url()`
(`dataone_standardize.R`), restricting requests to `https://pasta.lternet.edu` and
`https://pasta.edirepository.org` (EDI's own alternate system host for the same
infrastructure). Both call sites now skip (with a clear message/skip-reason) rather than
request any URL outside this allowlist. 6 new tests
(`test-dataone_standardize.R`, `test-dataone_preview.R`) cover accepted hosts, rejected
hosts (including a cloud metadata-endpoint address and `localhost`), non-`https` schemes,
and unparseable input.

**Zip-slip (Low, hardened defensively).** `download_gbif_occurrences.R`'s
`.read_gbif_zip()` called `utils::unzip()` with no entry-path validation. `zip_path`
originates from GBIF's own `occ_download()`/`occ_download_get()` API (a trusted first
party), so this was not assessed as exploitable today, but nothing re-validates that
trust downstream (cache tampering, a MITM'd download). Added an explicit entry-path check
(rejects absolute paths and `..` traversal segments) before extraction, as defense in
depth.

Everything else checked and found not exploitable (command injection: none found anywhere
in the package; XXE: `xml2::read_xml()` does not resolve external entities by default,
confirmed with a live test; unsafe deserialization: all `readRDS()` calls load only the
package's own previously-written cache files; path traversal: all user/API-derived
filename components are sanitized via `basename()` + character-class stripping before use
in `file.path()`; PDF magic-byte validation: confirmed working as documented, not
bypassable via extension alone).

# Domain Review

Purpose: To ensure the code produces outputs, data, interfaces, or software that is
biologically reasonable when compared to other similar information available.

### [x] Scientific Rigor: One real finding, fixed; two lower-severity findings fixed.

**Homonym misresolution in `get_keys_from_context()`'s `HIGHERRANK` recovery path
(Medium-High, fixed).** The function's entire design premise is that supplying full
taxonomic hierarchy context to GBIF's `name_backbone()` prevents homonym errors (its own
documented example: *Alaria* is both a brown alga and a trematode worm). But its recovery
path for a `HIGHERRANK` result too coarse to trust (`.recover_higherrank()`) called
`rgbif::name_lookup()` with only the name and rank -- no kingdom/phylum context -- and
picked the majority-vote `nubKey` across whatever checklist datasets `name_lookup()`
searched. This reintroduces exactly the failure mode the rest of the function exists to
prevent. Verified live against real GBIF data for *Alaria*: `name_lookup()` results mixed
kingdoms (Animalia/Platyhelminthes, Chromista/Ochrophyta, and others) under the same
generic-rank query, with the per-record `kingdom` field itself inconsistently populated
across checklist datasets -- confirming the concern is real, though also surfacing that
GBIF's backbone occasionally collapses distinct kingdoms to the same `nubKey` regardless
(a GBIF data-quality limitation outside this package's control, disclosed in the fixed
function's own roxygen).

*Decision (K. D. Lafferty): filter `name_lookup()` hits by kingdom before voting.* Fixed:
`.recover_higherrank()` now accepts a `context` list (the row's own already-available
hierarchy values) and narrows lookup hits to the matching kingdom before the majority
vote, falling back to the previous unfiltered behavior when no kingdom context is
available or the narrowed set is empty. The resulting `matchType = "LOOKUP_RECOVERED"`
was also missing from the function's documented `matchType` enum and its "review these
rows" advice -- both fixed. 3 new tests using a synthetic, deliberately unambiguous mixed-
kingdom fixture (real GBIF data was tried first but is too noisy to isolate the narrowing
logic cleanly, per the note above).

**BioTime `occurrenceStatus` conflated missing data with confirmed absence (Medium,
fixed).** `biotime_fetch.R`'s `read_biotime_study()` coded `occurrenceStatus` as
`"present"` when `ABUNDANCE`/`BIOMAS` was a valid number `> 0`, and `"absent"` in every
other case -- including rows where both fields were missing or failed `as.numeric()`
coercion on malformed source data (silently caught by `suppressWarnings()`). This treats
"unparseable" the same as "confirmed non-detection," a real risk for a database (BioTime)
that is predominantly presence-based, where an `"absent"` row is unusual and consequential
for downstream occurrence priors. Fixed: `occurrenceStatus` is now `NA` when neither field
parses to a number, `"absent"` only when at least one field is a valid, explicit zero, and
`"present"` as before. A verbose-mode message reports the affected row count. 3 new tests.

**eDNA-exclusion pattern was overly broad (Low-Medium, fixed).** `filter_gbif_quality()`'s
`exclude_edna` filter matched the generic phrases `"bulk sample"` and `"water sample"`
against `samplingProtocol`/`occurrenceRemarks`/`preparations`, in addition to
`"edna"`/`"environmental dna"`/`"metabarcod"`. The two generic phrases can appear in
non-eDNA methods (plankton tows, water-quality collection notes), risking silent exclusion
of legitimate presence data. Fixed: removed the two generic phrases from the pattern; real
GBIF eDNA datasets consistently self-label with one of the three remaining specific terms.
1 new test confirms generic wording alone no longer triggers exclusion.

### [x] Outputs: Comparable to other implementations; two doc-accuracy gaps fixed.

**`make_bbox_wkt()`'s km-conversion reference was latitude-dependent but undisclosed
(Low, doc fix).** The function always produces a square in degree-space (by design, not a
bug -- irregular polygons are explicitly routed to `TaxaTools::define_search_polygon()`
instead). Its docstring's "0.5 degrees is approximately 55 km" reference conversion holds
along the north-south axis only; east-west coverage shrinks by `cos(latitude)` and was not
disclosed, a real risk for high-latitude sites. Fixed: `@param radius_deg` now states the
caveat explicitly with concrete examples (about 78 km at 45 degrees, about 39 km at 70
degrees).

**`get_gbif_occurrences()`'s `rank_filter` default silently excludes subspecies-level
records (Low, doc fix, behavior unchanged).** `rank_filter = "species"` (default) is an
exact string match against `taxonRank`, so GBIF records ranked `SUBSPECIES`/`VARIETY`/
`FORM` are dropped even though they carry a usable species-level identity in their own
`species` column -- inconsistent with `filter_gbif_quality(require_species = TRUE)`'s more
permissive downstream check. Assessed as plausibly intentional (conservative default,
every existing caller already expects species-rank-only output) rather than a bug to fix
behaviorally this session; documented explicitly instead so the tradeoff is visible rather
than discovered by surprise.

### [x] Algorithms: Appropriate for intended purpose; no other flaws found.

`fetch_occurrences_by_taxon()`'s geometry union/combine logic, `stack_occurrences()`'s
`gbifID` dedup, `check_inat_range()`'s point-in-polygon logic, and the DataONE geo/taxon
LLM-screening prompts (deliberately biased toward "answer YES when in doubt," relying on
stricter downstream EML screening) were all read closely and found appropriate for their
purpose. `filter_gbif_quality()`'s other six filters (coordinates, absent-occurrence
exclusion, basis of record, issue codes, coordinate-uncertainty `NA`-handling, decimal-
place precision) are correctly implemented and match their documentation.

# File specific comments

- `R/dataone_standardize.R` -- added `.pasta_trusted_hosts` / `.is_trusted_pasta_url()`
  and the `.download_data_table()` guard (SSRF fix); `.recover_higherrank()` gained a
  `context` parameter and kingdom-narrowing logic (homonym fix); `.process_gbif_row()`
  updated to pass context through.
- `R/dataone_preview.R` -- `.preview_one_entity()` gained the same host-allowlist guard
  before its HEAD/stream calls.
- `R/get_keys_from_context.R` -- `matchType` roxygen enum and review-advice list updated
  to include `"LOOKUP_RECOVERED"`; summary message now reports a `LOOKUP_RECOVERED` count
  when nonzero.
- `R/biotime_fetch.R` -- `occurrenceStatus` derivation and all three related roxygen
  sections (`@details`, `@return` field, verbose summary message) updated for the
  NA-vs-absent distinction.
- `R/filter_gbif_quality.R` -- `edna_pattern` narrowed; inline comment explains why.
- `R/make_bbox_wkt.R` -- `@param radius_deg` gained the latitude-dependent caveat.
- `R/get_gbif_occurrences.R` -- `@param rank_filter` gained the exact-match/subspecies
  caveat. (Unrelated: this edit shifted `.lintr`'s line-293 `commented_code_linter`
  exclusion to line 300 -- updated; see `.lintr`'s Pass 5 note in the project's own
  pre-review-checklist memory about exclusion line-number drift.)
- `R/download_gbif_occurrences.R` -- `.read_gbif_zip()` gained a zip-slip entry-path
  check before extraction.
- `.lintr` -- added an `object_usage_linter` exclusion for `dataone_preview.R:544`
  (`.is_trusted_pasta_url()` cross-file call, same false-positive class as the existing
  `get_gbif_occurrences.R:217` exclusion, confirmed via `codetools::checkUsage()` on the
  loaded namespace).
- New/expanded test files: `test-dataone_standardize.R` (+6), `test-dataone_preview.R`
  (new file, +4 -- this file previously had zero test coverage at all;
  `preview_dataone_occurrences()` itself remains untested beyond this guard, a
  pre-existing gap out of scope for this review), `test-get_keys_from_context.R` (+3),
  `test-biotime_fetch.R` (+2), `test-filter_gbif_quality.R` (+1).
